subject: Modular SLA & annual discount request — pricing and ramp plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@pritech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pritech.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: modular SLA pricing + annual discount possibility

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers look great. Procurement and engineering at PriTech want to move quickly but have two primary asks before we can push this up to legal/finance: a modular SLA option (we want to mix uptime tiers across services) and clarity on annualized discounts for committed spend. Specifics:
- We're evaluating a 12–24 month commercial commitment but want a phased rollout: pilot (3 months) -> ramp (months 4–6) -> full production.
- We need separate sizing/pricing for: API text generation (high-throughput), embeddings (large index), and failover capacity (geo redundancy).
- Can you provide a simple matrix showing uptime tiers, response time SLAs, escalation coverage (who gets looped at what severity), and the discount schedule tied to annual commit?

Procurement is also asking for an initial ballpark on pilot pricing (we expect modest usage first month). Can you include any standard concessions for pilots?

Appreciate a one-page mutual action plan if possible. I've copied procurement; happy to set a 30-min call to go over.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure & Procurement
PriTech

Attachment: (none yet)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: modular SLA pricing + annual discount possibility

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline.

I've pulled together a concise SLA summary and an initial approach that maps modular tiers to the three workload buckets you called out. See attached SLA_Summary_v1.pdf (high level matrix + pilot concession). A few quick notes:
- We can support split-tier SLAs by route (e.g., embeddings vs generation) and bill per-route consumption in the tiered matrix.
- Pilot concession: standard is 50% off platform fees for the first 3 months for new enterprise pilots (applies to hosted API consumption, not pass-through cloud costs).
- Annualized discounts scale with committed TCV; options include 12/24/36-month commit steps.

Looping in Jordan for the pricing matrix and Laura for billing/prorate details. Rishi can confirm operational coverage (on-call, escalation windows, runbook access).

Next steps I propose: 30-min pricing & procurement call Wed or Thu, and we draft a 1-page mutual action plan (I can seed this). If that works for procurement, send a couple time options and we'll lock it.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: SLA_Summary_v1.pdf (PDF, 260KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pritech.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: modular SLA pricing + annual discount possibility

Samir — adding the pricing scaffolding here so procurement has concrete numbers to react to. High level (ballpark USD, list pricing before discount):

Uptime tiers (per-service):
- Bronze: 99.9% uptime, response time ( Sev2 ): 4 hours, base retainer $0
- Silver: 99.95% uptime, response time ( Sev2 ): 1 hour, retainer $3,000/month
- Gold: 99.99% uptime, response time ( Sev2 ): 15 minutes, retainer $12,500/month + 1 senior on-call rotation

Surge protection (hot standby capacity across two regions): add-on $8,000/month (includes 10M token burst capacity; overage billing at $X per M tokens).

Discount schedule (applied to Redwood platform fees only):
- 12-month commit: 10% off list
- 24-month commit: 18% off list
- 36-month commit: 25% off list

Pilot concession (what Sofia mentioned): 50% off platform fees for first 3 months. For procurement-friendly offers we can convert the pilot discount into an early-commit bonus (e.g., 3 months waived if you sign 24-month within pilot).

Billing/proration notes (Laura — please confirm but roughly): platform fees prorated to day-of-signature; retainer billed monthly in arrears; any credit for downtime calculated against monthly platform fees per SLA credit matrix.

If you want a blended deal across the three buckets (generation + embeddings + failover) we can provide a model with weighted usage assumptions — happy to run one if you share expected monthly tokens/embedding units for pilot.

Link to the DocuSign template I referenced: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123-SLA

Jordan Blake
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0134

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pritech.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: modular SLA pricing + annual discount possibility

Samir — quick operational clarifications on escalation and failover so procurement and engineering align on expectations:

- Severity definitions: Sev1 (service down / production impact) = immediate paging; Sev2 (degraded performance) = 1-hour target response for Silver, 15-min for Gold.
- Escalation roster: initial triage handled by Redwood Support (tier 1); Sev1 escalates to on-call engineer + an assigned SR (redwood solutions rep) within 30 minutes for Gold tier.
- Runbook & connectivity: customers on Gold receive read-only access to the runbook and a shared Slack/Teams channel for Sev1 incidents.
- Geo failover: Surge protection uses active-passive failover across two regions; cold-start failover time depends on KV cache rehydration (we estimate ~90–180s for small models, up to ~2 minutes for large KV sets).
- Limitations: Pilot will run on provisioned shared capacity unless you opt for dedicated capacity (which has a different pricing profile).

If you can share expected QPS and embedding index sizes for pilot I'll produce a short SRE note mapping failover RTO/RPO to the SLA tier.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Samir Patel <samir@pritech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pritech.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: modular SLA pricing + annual discount possibility

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround, this is helpful. A few items from procurement/engineering after review:

1) Discounting — PriTech would prefer a stronger 12-month offer given we want flexibility: proposal is 15% off list for a 12-month commit (with an option to extend to 24 months at 20% by month 9). We can move faster if you convert the pilot concession into a 3-month credit rather than just a percentage.

2) Pilot clarity — procurement asks that the pilot pricing be a capped monthly spend (e.g., $15k cap/month) rather than open-ended percentage discounts. That cap would make sign-off easier.

3) Billing/proration — please confirm if retainers are billed upfront or monthly; procurement would prefer retainers billed monthly in arrears and platform fees prorated at signature with invoice references.

4) MAP — can you seed a one-page mutual action plan that lists milestones, acceptance criteria for pilot, and decision points? If so, please include in the next email.

I've attached our standard procurement redlines for reference (Procurement_Terms_v3.docx). If you can get a one-pager + a revised pricing snapshot that includes the capped pilot spend and the alternate 12-month 15% concession by EOD Monday, we'll book a follow-up to finalize.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure & Procurement
PriTech
